captions: {city} sees measurable rain on about {total} days a year, most often in {peak}. Damp ground is what subterranean termites need to keep foraging, and the wetter stretches are when moisture-seeking insects — roaches, silverfish, centipedes — push in toward kitchens, bathrooms and crawl spaces.

Rain falls on roughly {total} days a year in {city}, {SS}, peaking in {peak} and easing to {low_value} in {low}. Insects lose water through their shells, so the number of damp days sets how long they can stay active and how far from shelter they will travel.

{city} records measurable rain on about {total} days a year. The wet stretches matter more than the totals — repeated wetting keeps soil and structural timber damp enough for termites to keep working, and it is damp timber rather than rainfall that decides where they go.
